aspects.says: Whether a worker has ended is a question for isAlive(); a worker waiting for work is WAITING or TIMED_WAITING and alive.
basis: section:A Thread Runs Once: Run the Work Again on a New Thread

aspects.says: join(millis) returns the same way whether or not the thread ended, so the caller asks isAlive() (or uses join(Duration)'s answer) before treating the work as done.
basis: section:join(millis) Returns Without Saying Why, So Ask isAlive()

aspects.says: An exception thrown in a started thread ends that thread only: join() returns normally and no catch of the caller runs, so the thread must hand the failure over, catching Throwable or through an UncaughtExceptionHandler.
basis: section:An Exception Ends Only Its Own Thread: Hand the Failure Over

aspects.says: start() and join() (or isAlive() returning false) are where a thread's data is handed over; a plain field polled while the thread runs carries no guarantee and its reader may spin forever.
basis: section:Results Come Back at join(): Start Every Worker, Then Join Every One
section:Spot the Problem: A Done Flag Instead of join()

aspects.says: join(0) waits forever, including when a deadline's remaining time rounds down to 0 ms; join(Duration) with zero or less only checks.
basis: section:join(millis) Returns Without Saying Why, So Ask isAlive()

aspects.says: Results are complete only after join() returns for every worker, and every worker is started before any is joined, so the work takes as long as the slowest one.
basis: section:Results Come Back at join(): Start Every Worker, Then Join Every One

aspects.says: start() returns before the new thread has run anything, so nothing the thread computes can be read on the caller's next line, and no order between the two threads holds after start().
basis: section:start() Doesn't Wait for the New Thread to Do Anything

aspects.says: start() is legal only on a NEW thread; to run the work again, a new Thread is created for the same Runnable.
basis: section:A Thread Runs Once: Run the Work Again on a New Thread

aspects.says: join(millis) on a thread that was never started returns at once and isAlive() is false, so the thread looks finished; join(Duration) throws IllegalThreadStateException instead.
basis: section:join(millis) Returns Without Saying Why, So Ask isAlive()
aspects.reason: it arises only in code handed a Thread it didn't start; the page shows the run, and the practices' code always starts its own threads, so a graded case would test an API corner rather than a decision the reader makes

aspects.says: A virtual thread is a daemon thread, so the JVM can exit before its work is done once main returns.
basis: section:start() Doesn't Wait for the New Thread to Do Anything
